speaker: Unknown
en: Good afternoon, everyone.
zh: 大家下午好。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's great to be here.
zh: 很高兴来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: We talk a lot about AI that lives on your screen, lives in the digital world.
zh: 我们经常谈论存在于你的屏幕上、存在于数字世界中的 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: And today I'd like to talk to you about a different kind of AI that we've been building at Waymo, AI that lives in the real physical world.
zh: 今天我想和你们谈谈我们在 Waymo 正在构建的一种不同的 AI，一种存在于真实物理世界中的 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: How many of you, by the way, have been in a Waymo?
zh: 顺便问一下，你们有多少人坐过 Waymo？

speaker: Unknown
en: Just raise your arms.
zh: 只要举起你们的手。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow, okay, that is impressive.
zh: 哇，好吧，这令人印象深刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: Especially, I understand many of you are out of town.
zh: 特别是，我了解到你们很多人是从外地来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The folks who are visiting and have not had a chance to check out Waymo, I hope while you're here in the Bay Area, give it a try.
zh: 那些来访且还没有机会体验 Waymo 的人，我希望你们在旧金山湾区期间，试一试。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this being...
zh: 所以这是……

speaker: Unknown
en: A startup school, I structured this presentation as a sequence of lessons, seven lessons that we've learned over the years at Waymo around what it takes to build and safely ship today's most mature application of AI in the physical world, the Waymo driver.
zh: 一个创业学校，我把这个演讲构建为一系列课程，七年来我们在 Waymo 学到的教训，关于构建并安全交付当今物理世界中最成熟的 AI 应用所需的东西，Waymo driver。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me start with a short video.
zh: 让我以一个短视频开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a clip from a ride that I recently took in a Waymo with my kids.
zh: 这是我最近和我的孩子们乘坐 Waymo 时的一个片段。

speaker: Unknown
en: So as you see here, we're moving forward, we're proceeding through an intersection, and a couple of human drivers just decide to cut in right in front of us.
zh: 所以正如你们在这里看到的，我们正在向前移动，我们正在通过一个十字路口，几个人类司机决定就在我们前面加塞。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the Waymo driver reacted safely, reacted smoothly.
zh: Waymo driver 做出了安全的反应，做出了平稳的反应。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, so much so that the kids, my kids were preoccupied in the backseat, they didn't even notice that anything happened.
zh: 事实上，程度如此之高，以至于孩子们，我的孩子们在后座忙着别的事，他们甚至没有注意到发生了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to me, this was a pretty powerful moment.
zh: 对我来说，这是一个相当强有力的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been working on this technology and this product for close to two decades.
zh: 我在这个技术和这个产品上已经工作了接近二十年。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I just did something fairly important.
zh: 而我刚刚做了一件相当重要的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: It acted safely.
zh: 它安全地行动了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It kept my kids safe.
zh: 它让我的孩子们保持了安全。

speaker: Unknown
en: It kept everybody safe.
zh: 它让每个人都保持了安全。

speaker: Unknown
en: And nobody noticed.
zh: 而且没人注意到。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that I think will be a bit of a theme in general when it comes to physical AI.
zh: 我认为这大体上将是关于物理 AI 的一个主题。

speaker: Unknown
en: That the best AI moments will look like nothing happened.
zh: 最好的 AI 时刻看起来会像什么都没发生一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just the task got done safely and smoothly.
zh: 只是任务被安全且平稳地完成了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And these sort of moments where the Waymo driver kept everyone safe are happening daily across our fleet.
zh: 这些 Waymo driver 保持每个人安全的时刻每天都在我们的车队中发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, the Waymo driver is serving around 500 trips per week and driving over 4 million fully autonomous miles every week in 15 cities across the United States.
zh: 今天，Waymo driver 每周服务大约 500 次行程，并在全美 15 个城市每周驾驶超过 400 万英里的完全自动驾驶里程。

speaker: Unknown
en: For a comparison, that's over 300 years every week of an average American driver per year.
zh: 作为比较，这相当于每周超过 300 年的平均美国司机的年度驾驶量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the Waymo driver is accomplishing that with a superhuman safety record.
zh: Waymo driver 正以超人的安全记录实现这一目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what does it take to build and deploy an AI agent in the physical world at scale?
zh: 那么，在物理世界中大规模构建和部署一个 AI 智能体需要什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Now in Silicon Valley, there's a common mantra to move fast and break things.
zh: 现在在硅谷，有一个常见的信条是快速行动并打破事物。

speaker: Unknown
en: However, when you're dealing with atoms instead of bits, breaking things is not really okay.
zh: 然而，当你处理的是原子而不是比特时，打破事物并不是真的可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the thing you have to do is to move fast and ship safely.
zh: 所以你必须做的事情是快速行动并安全交付。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's a much more difficult thing to do.
zh: 那是一件更难做到的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to build systems that are robust from day one.
zh: 你必须构建从第一天起就坚固的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to build AI models and you have to build training recipes where safety is the foundation and not an afterthought, not an add-on.
zh: 你必须构建 AI 模型，你必须构建训练配方，其中安全是基础，而不是事后考虑，不是附加组件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by the way, the problem itself of physical AI is different from digital AI.
zh: 顺便说一句，物理 AI 本身的问题与数字 AI 不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are four main gaps that you have to contend with if you're building AI for the physical world versus the digital world.
zh: 如果你是为物理世界而不是数字世界构建 AI，你必须应对四个主要的差距。

speaker: Unknown
en: First, there is the cost of error gaps.
zh: 首先，存在错误的代价差距。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you have a language model or a chatbot or a copilot and it makes a mistake, usually it costs you a retry.
zh: 如果你有一个语言模型或聊天机器人或副驾驶并且它犯了一个错，通常代价是你重试一次。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the physical world, the cost of a mistake can be measured in human lives, not tokens.
zh: 在物理世界，一个错误的代价可以用人类生命来衡量，而不是 tokens。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's simply not an undo and a retry button.
zh: 简单地没有一个撤销和重试按钮。

speaker: Unknown
en: Secondly, you have the latency gap.
zh: 其次，你有延迟差距。

speaker: Unknown
en: And typically, when you're running a vLM or a digital assistant, it can take many seconds, sometimes minutes, to come back with an answer to you.
zh: 通常，当你运行一个 vLM 或数字助手时，可能需要许多秒，有时几分钟，才能给你一个答复。

speaker: Unknown
en: A car traveling at freeway speeds moves about 100 feet in one second.
zh: 一辆以高速公路速度行驶的汽车在一秒内移动大约 100 英尺。

speaker: Unknown
en: So their milliseconds really matter.
zh: 所以那些毫秒真的很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you have to run all of your inference, make all of your decisions on board a compute that fits in the trunk of your car.
zh: 你必须在车上运行你所有的推理，在适合你汽车后备箱的计算设备上做出你所有的决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: Next, there's the data gap.
zh: 接下来，有数据差距。

speaker: Unknown
en: Digital AI had the internet of this wonderful, immense cache of pre-labeled human knowledge and human thought that we've ever assembled.
zh: 数字 AI 拥有互联网这个美妙的、巨大的预标记人类知识和人类思想的缓存，我们曾经组装过的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no digitized version of the internet for the physical world.
zh: 物理世界没有互联网的数字化版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And lastly, there's the validation gap.
zh: 最后，存在验证差距。

speaker: Unknown
en: In digital AI, often you can ship something that's good enough.
zh: 在数字 AI 中，你通常可以发布足够好的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you let your users use your product, they find the edge cases, and that allows you to deploy on day one practically at unlimited scale.
zh: 然后你让你的用户使用你的产品，他们会发现边缘情况，这让你能够在第一天实际上以无限制的规模进行部署。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you can just iterate and hill climb on quality from there.
zh: 然后你就可以从那里迭代并在质量上进行爬山。

speaker: Unknown
en: In physical AI, the situation is different.
zh: 在物理 AI 中，情况是不同的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Given the high cost of errors,
zh: 鉴于错误的高成本，

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to have a very high level of safety and a very high level of confidence on day one before you deploy your first robot, before you drive your first autonomous mile.
zh: 你需要在第一天拥有非常高水平的安全性和非常高水平的信心，在你部署第一个机器人之前，在你驾驶第一个自动驾驶里程之前。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, at the same time, when you're dealing with physical AI,
zh: 现在，与此同时，当你在处理物理 AI 时，

speaker: Unknown
en: The actual experience of having your agent in the real world is invaluable and it's irreplaceable.
zh: 让你的智能体处于现实世界的实际经验是无价的，并且它是不可替代的。

speaker: Unknown
en: These systems are not just something that you can build in the lab, get it perfect, and then deploy at full scale overnight.
zh: 这些系统不仅仅是那种你可以在实验室里构建、让它完美、然后一夜之间全面部署的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So given those two factors, you really need...
zh: 所以考虑到这两个因素，你真的需要……

speaker: Unknown
en: To super clearly and super crisply define the operating conditions and the deployment parameters of your agent, and then build a rigorous framework to guide your deployment so that you can scale in a responsible manner.
zh: 超级清晰和超级明确地定义你的智能体的运行条件和部署参数，然后建立一个严格的框架来指导你的部署，这样你就可以以一种负责任的方式进行扩展。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is absolutely critical.
zh: 而这是绝对关键的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is how you earn trust from your customers, from the communities, from the regulators, and yourself.
zh: 这就是你从你的客户、从社区、从监管机构以及你自己那里赢得信任的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So at Waymo, we see these gaps, of course, in the context of autonomous vehicles, but these gaps will show up in practically any sort of non-trivial physical agent that we will deploy in some shape or form.
zh: 所以在 Waymo，我们当然在自动驾驶汽车的背景下看到了这些差距，但这些差距实际上会出现在我们将以某种形式部署的几乎任何非平凡的物理智能体中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And driving is simply the first domain where AI has crossed these four gaps at scale with the public interacting with our product.
zh: 而驾驶只是 AI 在大规模上跨越这四个差距的第一个领域，并且公众与我们的产品进行互动。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's dive into those lessons that we've learned over the years at Waymo from working on this problem and talk about how we address those gaps.
zh: 所以让我们深入探讨多年来我们在 Waymo 从解决这个问题中学到的那些教训，并谈谈我们如何解决这些差距。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have seven lessons in this talk.
zh: 我在这次演讲中有七个教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're all technical.
zh: 它们全都是技术性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot more that goes into building a company and building a product, but today I'll just focus on the technical aspects of building AI for the physical world.
zh: 建立一家公司和建立一个产品还有更多的事情要做，但今天我将只专注于为物理世界构建 AI 的技术方面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And...
zh: 并且……

speaker: Unknown
en: Each one of those lessons, I think by itself, will not be exactly earth-shattering.
zh: 我认为这些教训中的每一个本身都不会是惊天动地的。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of it will overlap with likely things you've heard elsewhere.
zh: 其中很多会与你可能在其他地方听到的事情重叠。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I hope that the grounding of these lessons in our experience and some of the nuance that I can add about how they showed up in our experience of deploying a physical agent and scaling it safely will be interesting and useful for many of you who are in the space as you build your product, as you build your startup.
zh: 但我希望这些教训在我们经验中的基础，以及我可以补充的关于它们如何出现在我们部署物理智能体和进行安全扩展的经验中的细微差别，对于那些在这个领域中的许多人来说，当你们构建产品、构建初创公司时，将是有趣和有用的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's dive in.
zh: 所以让我们开始吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first lesson has to do with this massive, frustrating, sometimes soul-crushing difference between a demo and a real product.
zh: 第一个教训与这种巨大的、令人沮丧的、有时令人崩溃的演示和真实产品之间的差异有关。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a working demo is 1% at best of the work that you have to do.
zh: 而一个可运行的演示最多只是你必须做的工作的 1%。

speaker: Unknown
en: The many nines of performance, the many nines of reliability that follow, that's where the real work happens.
zh: 随后的许多个 9 的性能，许多个 9 的可靠性，那就是真正工作发生的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you're a founder in the room, chances are you are focused on getting that first prototype, that first demo off the ground.
zh: 如果你是房间里的一位创始人，很可能你正专注于让第一个原型、第一个演示起飞。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you hit that first version of a system that works, that first 90%, when the demo actually works, it feels incredible.
zh: 当你达到了系统的第一个可运行的版本，第一个 90%，当演示真正起作用时，感觉棒极了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You feel like you solved it.
zh: 你感觉你解决了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: The sky's the limit.
zh: 天空是极限。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're extrapolating forward.
zh: 你正在向前外推。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in our world, we hit that first milestone, that first 90%, back around 2010.
zh: 而在我们的世界里，我们在 2010 年左右达到了那个第一个里程碑，第一个 90%。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when this project started in 2009, before we started building the system, we set a couple of pretty ambitious goals for ourselves.
zh: 所以当这个项目在 2009 年开始时，在我们开始构建系统之前，我们为自己设定了几个相当雄心勃勃的目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: One was to drive 100,000 miles in autonomous mode.
zh: 一个目标是以自动驾驶模式驾驶 10 万英里。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second goal was to drive 10 routes.
zh: 第二个目标是驾驶 10 条路线。

speaker: Unknown
en: Each one was 100 miles long, chosen to cover a variety of conditions across the Bay Area.
zh: 每一条长 100 英里，被选中以覆盖跨越湾区地区的各种条件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we had to do each one from beginning to end without a human intervention.
zh: 我们必须在没有人工干预的情况下从头到尾完成每一条。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had at the time a team of about a dozen engineers, and we accomplished both of these goals in about a year and a half.
zh: 当时我们有一个大约十几名工程师的团队，我们在大约一年半的时间里实现了这两个目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: And keep in mind, this was well before any of the AI breakthroughs, before ConvNest, before Transformers, before BLMs, before any of the stuff that we talk about today.
zh: 并且请记住，这远在任何 AI 突破之前，在 ConvNest、Transformers、BLMs 之前，在我们今天谈论的任何东西之前。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yet, we got it done.
zh: 然而，我们完成了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by demo standards, autonomous driving was solved in 2010.
zh: 按照演示的标准，自动驾驶在 2010 年就被解决了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We handled everything.
zh: 我们处理了一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: We could drive during the day, during the night.
zh: 我们可以在白天、夜间驾驶。

speaker: Unknown
en: We handled traffic, pedestrians, cyclists, traffic lights, construction zones, on freeways, on surface streets.
zh: 我们处理了交通、行人、骑行者、红绿灯、施工区域、在高速公路上、在城市街道上。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we were, quote unquote, capability complete.
zh: 所以我们是，所谓的，能力完整的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at the time, we felt like we were on top of the world.
zh: 当时，我们感觉我们站在世界之巅。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then we quickly ran, as we started building towards the product, we quickly ran into a brutal reality that there's a massive difference between doing something once or driving 10 routes once and building a scalable service with nobody behind the wheel.
zh: 但随后我们很快碰到了，当我们开始向产品构建时，我们很快遇到了一个残酷的现实，那就是做一次某事或驾驶 10 条路线一次与建立一个没有人坐在方向盘后面的可扩展服务之间存在巨大差异。

speaker: Unknown
en: It took us about 10 more years.
zh: 我们花了大约又 10 年时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: To begin providing a service and then five more years to scale to half a million trips per week.
zh: 去开始提供服务，然后再花 5 年时间扩大规模到每周 50 万次行程。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the demo took 18 months, the product took about 15 years.
zh: 所以演示花了 18 个月，产品花了大约 15 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: But now we're scaling exponentially.
zh: 但现在我们正在指数级扩展。

speaker: Unknown
en: To date, we've served well over 20 million fully autonomous trips, and we've driven well over 200 million fully autonomous miles.
zh: 迄今为止，我们已经提供了超过 2000 万次完全自动驾驶的行程，并且我们已经行驶了超过 2 亿英里的完全自动驾驶里程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we have rider-only vehicles operating in 15 cities across the United States.
zh: 我们有仅限乘客的车辆在美国的 15 个城市运营。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're scaling exponentially.
zh: 我们正在指数级扩展。

speaker: Unknown
en: 15 years to get to that first 100 million miles and about seven months to drive the next 100 million.
zh: 花了 15 年时间才达到前 1 亿英里，而只用了大约七个月就行驶了下一个 1 亿英里。

speaker: Unknown
en: It took us about eight years to go from the time when we started our initial rider-only operation to the time when we were serving riders in four cities.
zh: 我们花了大约八年时间，从我们开始最初的仅限乘客运营之时，到我们在四个城市服务乘客之时。

speaker: Unknown
en: Earlier this year, we launched four cities in just one day.
zh: 今年早些时候，我们在仅仅一天内就在四个城市发布了服务。

speaker: Unknown
en: So why does bridging that gap from demo to product take so long?
zh: 那么为什么弥合从演示到产品之间的差距要花这么长时间？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because there's this harsh engineering reality that you can't really cheat that reliability and performance lives on this exponential ladder of nines.
zh: 因为有一个严酷的工程现实，你无法真正作弊，即可靠性和性能存在于这个指数级的"九"的阶梯上。

speaker: Unknown
en: So getting to that first 90% or 99%, that's the easy part.
zh: 所以达到第一个 90% 或 99%，那是容易的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then every next nine that you wanna add, that takes about 10 times more effort.
zh: 但随后你想增加的每一个"九"，那需要花费大约 10 倍的努力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you need to know upfront exactly how many nines your product actually needs.
zh: 所以你需要预先确切地知道你的产品实际上需要多少个"九"。

speaker: Unknown
en: So demo might need one nine, an assist product or Copilot might need a few, but a fully autonomous AI agent that we're gonna be putting out in the physical world that engages with the public and with kids running around, that needs a whole stack of them.
zh: 所以演示可能需要一个"九"，一个辅助产品或 Copilot 可能需要几个，但是一个我们要投放到现实世界中、与公众和周围跑来跑去的孩子们互动的完全自主的 AI 智能体，那需要整整一摞"九"。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at scale,
zh: 并且在大规模下，

speaker: Unknown
en: The long tail is the problem space.
zh: 长尾就是问题空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's your entire problem statement.
zh: 它就是你整个问题陈述。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you drive millions of miles per week, a rare event that might happen once in a million miles, that just becomes your daily reality.
zh: 当你每周行驶数百万英里时，一百万英里才发生一次的罕见事件，就变成了你的日常现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: And getting those next nines
zh: 而获得那些接下来的"九"

speaker: Unknown
en: It means doing something different every time.
zh: 这意味着每次都要做不同的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you don't get to say six nines of performance or reliability by doing the same thing that you did to achieve the first two, but longer.
zh: 所以你不能通过做与达到前两个"九"相同的事情但持续时间更长，就说你达到了六个九的性能或可靠性。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to do fundamentally different things.
zh: 你必须做根本性不同的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: It requires a fundamentally different approach.
zh: 它需要一种根本性不同的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, we can take reliability.
zh: 例如，我们可以拿可靠性来说。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can get to the first couple of nines by just doing proper engineering and doing some bug fixes.
zh: 你可以通过只是做正确的工程工作和做一些错误修复来达到前几个"九"。

speaker: Unknown
en: But to get to the next few, you need to invest in fundamentally different approaches.
zh: 但要达到接下来的几个，你需要投资于根本性不同的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to build fully redundant systems, have tiered fallback architectures, and so forth and so on.
zh: 你需要构建完全冗余的系统，拥有分层的降级架构等等等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the same thing holds for the performance of AI models.
zh: 并且对于 AI 模型的性能也是如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what that actually means is that in this space, it's incredibly easy to get started, but it can be excruciatingly difficult to get to the real product.
zh: 所以这实际上意味着在这个领域，开始极其容易，但要做成真正的产品可能极其困难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that effect is only amplified with every wave of technological breakthroughs.
zh: 而这种效应随着每一次技术突破的浪潮只会被放大。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that naturally leads to hype cycles.
zh: 这自然导致了炒作周期。

speaker: Unknown
en: So every AI breakthrough from deep learning to condom nets to transformers, VLMs, you name it, it makes it that much easier to get started.
zh: 所以每一次 AI 突破，从深度学习到 condom nets 再到 transformers、VLMs，等等，都让开始变得容易得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your demos, your prototypes, they get 100 times easier.
zh: 你的演示，你的原型，它们变得容易了 100 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the tail, that's where the hard problems are, that moves much less.
zh: 但是尾部，那是棘手问题所在的地方，那个地方移动得少得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: It moves, but the effect is muted.
zh: 它在移动，但效果被削弱了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's why every hype cycle produces a wave of absolutely spectacular demos and very few real products.
zh: 这就是为什么每一个炒作周期都会产生一波绝对精彩的演示，却很少有真正的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the recurring mistake of every cycle is spending on the demo what you should be saving for the nines.
zh: 每一个周期反复出现的错误是，把你应该留给那些"九"的资源花在了演示上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, this being a startup school, the last thing I want to do is throw too much cold water on the magic and the excitement of those early days.
zh: 现在，鉴于这是初创学校，我最不想做的就是给那些早期日子的魔力和兴奋泼太多冷水。

speaker: Unknown
en: This time is absolutely magical.
zh: 这段时间绝对是充满魔力的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's amazing.
zh: 它棒极了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cherish it.
zh: 珍惜它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Leverage it.
zh: 利用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the key is to remain honest about the product that you're building, the number of nines and performance and reliability that that product demands, and not cutting corners to get there.
zh: 但关键在于对你正在构建的产品保持诚实，即该产品对"九"的数量、性能和可靠性的要求，并且在达到目标时不偷工减料。

speaker: Unknown
en: Otherwise, you might be in for a pretty rude awakening later.
zh: 否则，你以后可能会遭遇相当猛然的惊醒。

speaker: Unknown
en: So count your nines before you count your demo views.
zh: 所以在统计你的演示浏览量之前，先计算你的"九"。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this brings us to the second lesson.
zh: 这给我们带来了第二个教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once you know how many nines your product actually needs, it fundamentally dictates the architecture and the core technical approach that you need to pursue.
zh: 一旦你知道你的产品实际上需要多少个"九"，它从根本上就决定了你需要追求的架构和核心技术方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, every technology has a performance versus effort curve, right?
zh: 现在，每一种技术都有一个性能与投入的曲线，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: They all tend to start fairly steep and go up, and then they flatten out.
zh: 它们往往起步都很陡峭并向上延伸，然后变平。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as I just mentioned, every other nine gets an order of magnitude more difficult.
zh: 正如我刚才提到的，每增加一个 9，难度就会增加一个数量级。

speaker: Unknown
en: So common failure mode is picking the tech that gives you the fastest early ramp, riding that steep curve, feeling like you're winning, projecting that steep slope into the future and feeling like the sky is the limit, and then hitting the plateau and discovering that the technology path that you picked actually flattens out way before the performance that is required by your product.
zh: 常见的失败模式是选择了那些能给你最快早期爬坡的技术，驾驭那段陡峭的曲线，感觉像是赢了，将那个陡峭的斜坡投射到未来并感觉天空才是极限，然后撞上高原，发现你选择的技术路径实际上在产品所需的性能之前很早就变平了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, you might still choose to be, at least for a while, on that steep curve for a variety of practical reasons.
zh: 现在，出于各种实际原因，你可能仍然选择至少在一段时间内处于那条陡峭的曲线上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe you want to prototype something or demo something or build something in service of learning, but be honest with yourself where you're building for the purpose of a demo, for the purpose of learning, or towards an actual product.
zh: 也许你想制作原型或演示某些东西，或者为了学习而构建某些东西，但要诚实地面对自己，你是为了演示的目的、学习的目的，还是为了打造一个实际产品而构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's take an example from our domain, autonomous vehicle and sensing.
zh: 所以让我们从我们的领域——自动驾驶和感知——举个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's been a long-standing debate about what kind of sensors do you actually need for autonomous driving.
zh: 关于自动驾驶实际上需要什么样的传感器，一直存在长期的争论。

speaker: Unknown
en: Naturally, more sensors means higher performance, but also means higher complexity.
zh: 当然，更多的传感器意味着更高的性能，但也意味着更高的复杂性。

speaker: Unknown
en: So humans...
zh: 所以人类……

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course, can drive with just eyes, so there's that proof of existence.
zh: 当然，只用眼睛就能驾驶，所以这就有了存在的证明。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, and if the goal were to just approximately match human performance or to build an assist product, that's a very reasonable way to go.
zh: 现在，如果目标只是大致匹配人类性能或构建辅助产品，那是一个非常合理的选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: However, if you are targeting full autonomy and you're targeting superhuman, strongly superhuman performance, you find that weak sensing just leads to a safety curve that flattens out way too early.
zh: 然而，如果你的目标是完全自动驾驶，且你的目标是超人、强超人性能，你会发现弱感知只会导致安全曲线过早变平。

speaker: Unknown
en: So at Waymo, we've taken an approach where we use multiple sensing modalities.
zh: 所以在 Waymo，我们采取了一种使用多种感知模态的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: We use cameras, lighters, and radars, and they all complement each other.
zh: 我们使用相机、打火机和雷达，它们互为补充。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cameras give you high resolution and color, but they're passive and they degrade in darkness and glare.
zh: 相机提供高分辨率和色彩，但它们是被动的，且在黑暗和眩光下性能会下降。

speaker: Unknown
en: LiDAR gives you a direct measurement of the 3D structure of the world around you.
zh: LiDAR 为你提供周围世界 3D 结构的直接测量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And radar is very good at punching through environmental conditions and weather like fog or rain or snow.
zh: 雷达非常擅长穿透环境条件和天气，如雾或雨或雪。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it directly can measure velocity using Doppler.
zh: 它可以直接利用多普勒测量速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: LiDAR and radar are active sensors.
zh: LiDAR 和雷达是主动传感器。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that means they see just as well in pitch darkness or, for example, when driving into a blinding sunset.
zh: 所以这意味着它们在漆黑一片或例如迎着刺眼的落日行驶时也能看得一样清楚。

speaker: Unknown
en: And these different sensing modalities, of course, they're not backups to each other.
zh: 当然，这些不同的感知模态并不是彼此的备份。

speaker: Unknown
en: In our stack, each modality has an encoder and the information from all of those sensors get fused into a single view of the world around us that is much more precise and generally vastly superior to what you get with any one sensor.
zh: 在我们的技术栈中，每个模态都有一个编码器，来自所有这些传感器的信息被融合成关于我们周围世界的单一视图，这比使用任何单一传感器获得的视图更精确，总体上要优越得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let me show you a few examples.
zh: 所以让我给你们看几个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's the scene where Waymo is driving in a dust storm in Phoenix.
zh: 这是 Waymo 在凤凰城的沙尘暴中行驶的场景。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what you see here is what the scene looks like to our fairly advanced high resolution and high dynamic range camera.
zh: 所以你在这里看到的是，场景在我们相当先进的高分辨率和高动态范围相机中的样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very close to what a human would see in the same conditions.
zh: 这与人类在相同条件下看到的景象非常接近。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which is not much.
zh: 也就是看不多远。

speaker: Unknown
en: And here on the right is what the LiDAR sees for the exact same frame.
zh: 这里右边是 LiDAR 在完全相同的帧中看到的景象。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can much more clearly see that there's a pedestrian standing on the side of the road.
zh: 你可以更清楚地看到有一个行人站在路边。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if they were to step onto the road, that early detection can make a really big difference in how the situation plays out and the safety of everyone involved.
zh: 所以如果他们踏上马路，这种早期检测可以在事态发展和相关人员的安全方面产生巨大的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's another example.
zh: 这是另一个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: At night, driving along, and there are a couple of pedestrians who are about to jump onto the road over a concrete construction barrier.
zh: 在晚上，正开着车，有几个行人正准备跳过一道混凝土施工屏障冲上马路。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, the bottom, you see the camera, really can't see much, and the lighter view at the top.
zh: 同样，底部你看到的是相机，真的看不了太多，而顶部是打火机视图。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, lighter versus camera.
zh: 同样，打火机对比相机。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's another example.
zh: 这是另一个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are a couple of dogs chasing a bull and a couple of kids chasing the dogs.
zh: 有几只狗在追赶一头公牛，还有几个小孩在追赶那些狗。

speaker: Unknown
en: And big difference.
zh: 区别很大。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's what it looks like to the camera.
zh: 这是相机看到的样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's the lighter.
zh: 这是打火机。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the early detection of the kids is off to the side.
zh: 而且对孩子们的早期检测是在侧面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there are no headlights.
zh: 没有前大灯。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are no lamps.
zh: 没有路灯。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is complete darkness.
zh: 一片漆黑。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it makes a big difference.
zh: 所以这产生了巨大的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or think about what happens when something physically obstructs the view of your sensors.
zh: 或者想一想当有物体物理阻挡你传感器视线时会发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you don't have redundancy in sensing, you can have a single leaf land on your sensors and bring your robot to a full stop.
zh: 如果你在感知上没有冗余，一片单片落在你的传感器上就可能让你的机器人完全停下。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you need redundancy.
zh: 所以你需要冗余。

speaker: Unknown
en: Redundancy, of course, does not necessarily mean multiple sensing modalities, but if you need redundancy anyway, you might as well benefit from the complementary physics of the different sensing modalities in the nominal case.
zh: 冗余不一定意味着多种感知模态，但如果你无论如何都需要冗余，你不妨在正常情况下受益于不同感知模态的互补物理特性。

speaker: Unknown
en: So here's a video of one of our cars that picked up a leaf or actually I think a full branch of a tree that our wipers were unable to shake and the car detected that and because we have sensing redundancy, it safely was able to get back to the depot for proper cleaning.
zh: 这里有一段我们其中一辆车的视频，它沾上了一片叶子，或者实际上我认为是一整根树枝，我们的雨刷无法甩掉，而车检测到了这一点，因为我们有感知冗余，它能够安全地返回车场进行适当的清洁。

speaker: Unknown
en: So specifically, when it comes to hardware,
zh: 所以具体来说，当谈到硬件时，

speaker: Unknown
en: Do not anchor to today's components prices.
zh: 不要锚定今天的组件价格。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are on the sixth generation of the Waymo driver, the Waymo hardware suite today.
zh: 我们正处于 Waymo 驾驶员的第六代，也就是今天的 Waymo 硬件套件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with every generation, the hardware not only delivered amazing capability, but we're able to drastically simplify and radically reduce the cost of the hardware as well.
zh: 而且每一代不仅提供了惊人的能力，而且我们还能够极大地简化并从根本上降低硬件的成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: So betting your company, betting your approach on today's hardware prices is just betting your company on a number that has a fairly short shelf life and is going to expire.
zh: 所以把你的公司、把你的方法押注在今天的硬件价格上，就是把你的公司押注在一个保质期相当短并且将要过期的数字上。

speaker: Unknown
en: So hardware will change.
zh: 所以硬件会改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: Many components will get commoditized and drop in price, so design for that future and be ready to upgrade.
zh: 许多组件将变得商品化并降价，所以要为那个未来设计，并准备好升级。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that brings us to the next lesson, lesson number three.
zh: 这就把我们带到了下一个教训，也就是第三课。

speaker: Unknown
en: Technology moves incredibly fast, especially nowadays.
zh: 技术发展得非常快，尤其是现在。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you need to be ready to ride those tech waves and do that repeatedly.
zh: 所以你需要准备好驾驭那些技术浪潮，并反复这样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you do, you have to not only think about the wins in performance and the wins in capability, you have to be very mindful about unification and simplification.
zh: 当你这样做时，你不仅要考虑性能上的胜利和能力上的胜利，你必须非常注意统一和简化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Over the years, we've seen a number of major breakthroughs in technology, a lot of them around AI.
zh: 这些年来，我们看到了许多重大的技术突破，其中许多是围绕 AI 的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with every wave of innovation, we pretty much rebuild the Waymo driver around that major wave of AI breakthroughs.
zh: 随着每一次创新的浪潮，我们几乎都围绕那波主要的 AI 突破重新构建了 Waymo 驾驶员。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we often push the state of the art in those areas forward ourselves.
zh: 并且我们经常自己推动这些领域的技术前沿。

speaker: Unknown
en: We leveraged ConvNets around 2013 for computer vision and perception.
zh: 我们在 2013 年左右利用了 ConvNets 进行计算机视觉和感知。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then when Transformers came about around 2017, we bet big on them both for perception and for the task of behavior prediction and decision making and planning.
zh: 然后在 2017 年左右 Transformers 出现时，我们不仅在感知方面，而且在行为预测、决策制定和规划任务上都对它们下了重注。

speaker: Unknown
en: Turns out the task of driving is not that dissimilar from the task of modeling language because of the social aspects of driving.
zh: 事实证明，由于驾驶的社会属性，驾驶任务与语言建模任务并没有那么不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're kind of having a conversation with other dynamic actors in the world, but you're doing that in the space, kind of body language of your agent, your car, as opposed to just the language of words.
zh: 你有点像是在与世界上其他动态参与者进行对话，但你是通过空间、通过你的智能体、你的汽车的肢体语言来做这件事，而不是仅仅通过语言文字。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you operate in sequences and local continuity matters, but so does global context.
zh: 并且你在序列中操作，局部的连续性很重要，但全局的上下文也很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And today we're leveraging the latest in VLMs and frontier role models.
zh: 今天我们正在利用最新的 VLMs 和前沿角色模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, using the latest tech for capability and performance wins, I don't want to say it's easy, but it can be reasonably straightforward.
zh: 现在，为了能力和性能的胜利而使用最新技术，我不想说这很容易，但它可能是相当直接的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Doing applied research in isolation or starting a tiger team to prototype some new technology is not the most difficult part.
zh: 孤立地做应用研究或启动一个老虎团队来原型化一些新技术并不是最困难的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's many companies, many teams that are excellent in this.
zh: 有许多公司、许多团队在这方面很出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: The much harder muscle to build is to carry that bleeding edge research into production and deploy it in a safety-critical environment without regressions.
zh: 更难构建的能力是将那项前沿研究投入生产，并在安全关键的环境中部署它而不出现回归。

speaker: Unknown
en: And do it without breaking stride on the scaling of your product.
zh: 并且在不打断产品扩张步伐的情况下做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And adding capability, again, is not the hardest part, but adding capability while at the same time reducing fragmentation and reducing complexity, that is really important.
zh: 并且增加能力，再次强调，不是最困难的部分，但在增加能力的同时减少碎片化和减少复杂性，那才是真正重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And finally, the hard muscle to build as a company is to be able to do that repeatedly through multiple waves of technical innovation or technical breakthroughs.
zh: 最后，作为一家公司要建立的这种难能可贵的能力，是能够通过多次技术创新浪潮或技术突破反复做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So on this front, I have two bits of advice.
zh: 所以在这方面，我有两点建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first one, when the technology, a new technology shows up, it can be very exciting, very tempting to kick off a new effort, a tiger team to pursue it.
zh: 第一点，当一项新技术出现时，启动一项新的努力、一个老虎团队来追求它可能会非常令人兴奋，非常诱人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's great.
zh: 那很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: You should absolutely do that.
zh: 你绝对应该那样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: However, when you do, it's very important that you consider what you would do after.
zh: 然而，当你这样做时，考虑之后的后续工作是非常重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Under a success scenario, let's say that effort succeeds, you should be very clear on what the path of that new innovation is for your company, for your entire product, for your entire system.
zh: 在成功的情况下，假设那项努力成功了，你应该非常清楚那项新创新对你的公司、对你的整个产品、对你的整个系统的路径是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oftentimes, I've seen a failure mode where a project, a very difficult technical project succeeds, and then there's a dead end.
zh: 我经常看到一种失败模式，一个项目、一个非常困难的技术项目成功了，然后就走进了死胡同。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that can be very wasteful.
zh: 那样可能会非常浪费。

speaker: Unknown
en: That can be completely deflating.
zh: 那可能会完全令人泄气。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second bit of advice I have here is when pursuing new tech, again, don't just ask, what does this new tech give me in terms of capability and performance?
zh: 我在这里的第二点建议是，在追求新技术时，同样不要只问，这项新技术在能力和性能方面给了我什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Also ask, has it simplified my stack?
zh: 还要问，它简化了我的技术栈吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And has it led to fragmentation or unification?
zh: 以及它导致了碎片化还是统一？

speaker: Unknown
en: So set your launch bar to demand both breakthrough performance and at the same time, radical simplification and unification.
zh: 所以设定你的发布门槛，要求同时具备突破性的性能，以及根本性的简化和统一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this exact philosophy and this muscle that we've built at Waymo over the years is what produced our latest core technology.
zh: 正是这种确切的哲学和我们多年来在 Waymo 建立的能力，产生了我们最新的核心技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the heart of it is the Waymo Foundation Model.
zh: 它的核心就是 Waymo 基础模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, the Waymo Foundation Model is a multimodal world action language model.
zh: 现在，Waymo 基础模型是一个多模态世界动作语言模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's kind of a mouthful, so let me unpack the ingredients.
zh: 这名字有点拗口，所以让我来解析一下它的组成部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a multimodal model because it is able to process these multimodal sensory inputs, cameras, lighters, and radar.
zh: 它是一个多模态模型，因为它能够处理这些多模态感官输入，摄像头、打火机和雷达。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: And finally, it's aligned with language, and that allows us to unlock general world knowledge from visual language models.

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's incredibly useful in the long tail of rare semantic situations.

speaker: Unknown
en: So more specifically, this is what the architecture looks like.

speaker: Unknown
en: It's kind of your typical encoder-decoder architecture.
zh: 这是一种典型的编码器-解码器架构。

speaker: Unknown
en: The encoder part takes in the multimodal sensing and compresses it or encodes it into an efficient representation that retains all of the relevant data, all of the relevant information for the generative part or the decoder.
zh: 编码器部分接收多模态感知并将其压缩或编码成一种高效的表示，该表示保留了生成部分或解码器所需的所有相关数据，所有相关信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's an end-to-end model which has a couple of nice properties.
zh: 这是一个端到端模型，它有几个很好的特性。

speaker: Unknown
en: It allows us to effectively back propagate the gradient from the task that we actually care about all the way to the early layers of the model.
zh: 它使我们能够有效地将梯度从我们真正关心的任务反向传播一直传回模型的早期层。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it allows the encoder to learn the right rich representations for what the generative part needs to solve the task.
zh: 并且它允许编码器学习正确的丰富表示，以供生成部分解决任务所需。

speaker: Unknown
en: It uses a system one, system two, think fast, think slow architecture.
zh: 它使用了系统一，系统二，思考快，思考慢的架构。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 并且它利用 VLMs 的通用世界知识来高效学习语义任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's dive deeper.
zh: 所以让我们深入探讨。

speaker: Unknown
en: First, the think-fast path.

speaker: Unknown
en: That part fuses the raw data from our cameras, our lighters, our radars, and that allows for split-second safety-critical decisions.
zh: 那部分融合了来自我们摄像头、我们 lighters、我们雷达的原始数据，这使得毫秒级的安全关键决策成为可能。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can think of it as kind of your driving instincts.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 这就是允许汽车立即刹车的原因，比如说，如果行人跑上马路，或者附近的骑车人 svers 到你的路径上。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is like the lizard brain of your agent that deals with a lot of geometric tasks and can react in milliseconds.
zh: 这就像你智能体的蜥蜴大脑，它处理大量几何任务并且能在毫秒内做出反应。

speaker: Unknown
en: Second is the slow path.
zh: 第二是慢路径。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the part that's responsible for the more complex semantic and scene level understanding type tasks.
zh: 那是负责更复杂的语义和场景级理解类任务的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And these sort of tasks, these things don't typically change in milliseconds.
zh: 而且这类任务，这些事情通常不会在毫秒内发生变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there you can afford a bit more latency and you can trade that off for higher capability and higher levels of reasoning.
zh: 所以在那里你可以承受稍多一点延迟，并以此来换取更高的能力和更高水平的推理。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for example,
zh: 所以举个例子，

speaker: Unknown
en: If the Waymo driver encounters a situation when there's a vehicle, let's say it's on fire on the side of the road, the fast path might just see it as a generic obstacle and reason that the path ahead of us is clear.
zh: 如果 Waymo 驾驶员遇到一种情况，比如路边有一辆车着火了，快路径可能只会把它看作一个普通障碍物，并推断我们要走的路径是畅通的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is where the slow path comes in.
zh: 这就是慢路径介入的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that path can use deep semantic reasoning to understand the semantics of that object, the car being on fire, in the broader scene context.
zh: 那条路径可以使用深度语义推理来在更广泛的场景上下文中理解该对象的语义，那辆车着火了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that allows our driver to decide to take a very different action or a different route entirely, even if geometrically the path ahead of us is very unclear.
zh: 这使得我们的驾驶员能够决定采取截然不同的行动或完全不同的路线，即使在几何上我们要走的路径非常不清晰。

speaker: Unknown
en: And finally, there's the generate component.
zh: 最后，有一个生成组件。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the decoder.
zh: 那是解码器。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the component that understands and can produce behavior.
zh: 那是理解并能够产生行为的组件。

speaker: Unknown
en: It understands how other actors behave, and it allows us to make predictions and plan our own driving decisions.
zh: 它理解其他参与者如何行为，并且它允许我们进行预测并规划我们自己的驾驶决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: And our Waymo Foundation model powers the Waymo driver that runs on different generations of hardware and runs on different vehicle platforms.
zh: 我们的 Waymo 基础模型为 Waymo 驾驶员提供动力，它运行在不同世代的硬件上，并运行在不同的车辆平台上。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have our fifth generation, the sixth generation, the JLR IPAs, the Ojai, and the Hyundai Ioniq.
zh: 你有我们的第五代，第六代，JLR IPAs，Ojai，以及 Hyundai Ioniq。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in the future, we'll power different products and different commercial applications like trucking and personally owned vehicles.
zh: 在未来，我们将为不同的产品和不同的商业应用提供动力，如货运和私人拥有的车辆。

speaker: Unknown
en: So by...
zh: 所以通过……

speaker: Unknown
en: Leveraging the strategy of focusing on the high-capacity foundation of our model, we're able to move a lot of complexity upstream to that large shared foundation.
zh: 利用专注于我们模型高容量基础的策略，我们能够将大量复杂性向上游转移到那个大型共享基础。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that allows us to make that specialization layer that's running on the car pretty lightweight.
zh: 这使得我们能够使运行在车上的那个专业化层非常轻量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that in turn allows us to speed up the development process.
zh: 这反过来又使我们能够加速开发过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the most important muscle in this lesson is
zh: 所以这节课中最重要的肌肉是

speaker: Unknown
en: For your company to not just leverage the tech of the day, but have the ability and build that muscle to repeatedly ride those tech waves and pull in the results of that innovation into production without regression, without breaking stride in deployment and scaling, and without drowning in complexity.
zh: 你的公司不仅要利用当下的技术，还要有能力并建立那种肌肉，以反复驾驭这些技术浪潮，并将创新的结果引入生产，而无需回归，无需在部署和扩展中破坏步伐，且不会淹没在复杂性中。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's move to the next lesson.
zh: 所以让我们进入下一课。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is a well-known lesson in the AI community that
zh: AI 社区有一个众所周知的教训，那就是

speaker: Unknown
en: General methods that leverage massive compute and massive data will always beat methods that rely on handcrafted engineered human knowledge.
zh: 利用海量算力和海量数据的通用方法将总是胜过依赖手工设计的人类知识的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the so-called better lesson that Richard Sutton published and formulated in 2019.
zh: 这就是 Richard Sutton 在 2019 年发表和阐述的所谓的更好的教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we have lived this and we have seen this in every wave of technical breakthroughs.
zh: 我们经历过这一点，并在每一次技术突破的浪潮中都看到了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Each time the better lesson holds methods that scale best with compute, with data, they always win out.
zh: 每次更好的教训都成立，那些在算力、数据上扩展性最好的方法，它们总是获胜。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by the way, this is one of the reasons why we bet on the approach of building the foundation model.
zh: 顺便说一句，这就是我们押注于构建基础模型这一方法的原因之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is a well-known property that if you bet on high capacity model and you use your data and your compute on that, you just get better scaling laws and then you distill into smaller, more efficient models that are running on your agent in real time.
zh: 有一个众所周知的属性，如果你押注于高容量模型并在其上使用你的数据和算力，你只会得到更好的扩展定律，然后你蒸馏成更小、更高效的模型，这些模型在你的智能体上实时运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just get better scaling laws as opposed to just focusing on the smaller models directly.
zh: 你只是得到了更好的扩展定律，而不是仅仅直接专注于较小的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one nuanced area where this lesson shows up is the use of structure in your models.
zh: 所以这个教训出现的一个微妙领域是模型中结构的使用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And depending on how you use your structure, you can end up on either side of the bitter lesson.
zh: 根据你如何使用你的结构，你可能最终站在苦涩教训的任何一边。

speaker: Unknown
en: Essentially, structure that fights scale will always lose, and structure that channels scale always wins.
zh: 本质上，对抗规模的结构将总是输掉，而引导规模的结构将总是获胜。

speaker: Unknown
en: In particular, this comes up around the discussion of end-to-end models.
zh: 特别地，这出现在端到端模型的讨论中。

speaker: Unknown
en: As I mentioned, an end-to-end model has some very nice properties.
zh: 正如我提到的，端到端模型有一些非常好的特性。

speaker: Unknown
en: You back property gradient from the final tasks all the way through the model, and it allows the API between the encoder and decoder to use rich learn representations.
zh: 你从最终任务一路通过模型反向属性梯度，

speaker: Unknown
en: And those are the easiest models to build and train.
zh: 并且它允许编码器和解码器之间的 API 使用丰富的学习表征。

speaker: Unknown
en: The architectures are known.
zh: 并且这些是最容易构建和训练的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can start with doing some imitation learning and a kind of a black box end-to-end model will give you very rapid progress and you will ride that very initial steep part of the curve.
zh: 架构是已知的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for some products, that's enough.
zh: 你可以从做一些模仿学习开始，一种黑盒端到端模型会给你非常快速的进展，并且你会经历曲线那个非常初始的陡峭部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you need to reach superhuman levels of performance in a fully autonomous agent in a safety-critical environment, just doing kind of that basic vanilla end-to-end is not enough.
zh: 但是如果你需要在安全关键环境中的完全自主智能体中达到超人类水平的性能，仅仅做那种基本的原味端到端是不够的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is where structure comes in.
zh: 这就是结构介入的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the key question here is, does the structure boost scale or does it fight it?
zh: 这里的关键问题是，结构是提升规模还是对抗规模？

speaker: Unknown
en: Does it limit and constrain your solution space?
zh: 它是否限制并约束了你的解空间？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or does it help you scale without loss of generality?
zh: 或者它是否帮助你在不损失通用性的情况下扩展？

speaker: Unknown
en: So let me give you an example.
zh: 所以让我给你举个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me illustrate this point with kind of a simple thought exercise and a toy problem.
zh: 让我用一个简单的思想练习和一个玩具问题来说明这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Imagine you are building a robot that will play the game of Go.
zh: 想象你正在构建一个会下围棋的机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you want it to play the game in the physical world.
zh: 并且你希望它在物理世界中玩这个游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you have a camera that's observing the board and you have an actuator that will actually move the pieces around.
zh: 所以你有一个观察棋盘的摄像头，你有一个实际上会移动棋子的致动器。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, one way you can build such a robot is to have an end-to-end system that goes directly from pixels to actuation.
zh: 现在，构建这种机器人的一种方法是拥有一个直接从像素到致动的端到端系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And maybe you train it by giving it some videos of how humans play the game.
zh: 也许你通过给它一些人类如何玩这个游戏的视频来训练它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that could be a very interesting research exercise.
zh: 那可能是一个非常有趣的研究练习。

speaker: Unknown
en: However, if your goal was to build the world's best playing Go robot, that's probably not the most efficient way to go.
zh: 然而，如果你的目标是构建世界上最好的下围棋机器人，那可能不是最高效的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason for that is that there is a very simple...
zh: 原因是有一个非常简单的...

speaker: Unknown
en: Intermediate representation that captures completely the state of the game, the state of the task that you're trying to solve.
zh: 中间表示，它完全捕获了游戏的状态，你试图解决的任务的状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a 19 by 19 board.
zh: 它是一个 19x19 的棋盘。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that gives you a fully observable and complete state of the world that you care about, at least for the game planning part.
zh: 这给你提供了一个完全可观察和完整的世界状态，这是你所关心的，至少对于游戏规划部分而言。

speaker: Unknown
en: So leveraging that structure, it doesn't limit your model, it doesn't constrain your solution space, but it gives you a very helpful way to scale.
zh: 因此利用这种结构，它不限制你的模型，它不约束你的解空间，但它给你一种非常有帮助的扩展方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, that, of course, was a toy example.
zh: 现在，那当然是一个玩具例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anything that's not trivial that you're trying to deploy in the physical world will not have that property.
zh: 任何你试图在物理世界部署的非平凡事物都不会具有该属性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the fact that such a simple, clean, engineered representation doesn't exist in the physical world is the whole reason why we need end-to-end systems and learned representations and learned embeddings.
zh: 事实上，这种简单、干净、工程化的表示在物理世界中不存在，这就是我们需要端到端系统以及学习到的表示和学习到的嵌入的全部原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in the physical world, there does exist structure.
zh: 但在物理世界中，确实存在结构。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have laws of physics, you have rules of the road, you have objects that behave in reasonably predictable ways, and you can use that structure in addition to the learned representations to boost your performance, simplify validation, and at the end of the day, just get better scaling laws.
zh: 你有物理定律，你有交通规则，你有以相当可预测的方式表现的对象，你可以除了学习到的表示之外利用这种结构来提升你的性能，简化验证，归根结底，只是获得更好的缩放定律。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is the approach that we are pursuing at Waymo, which we call structure augmented end-to-end.
zh: 这是我们在 Waymo 正在追求的方法，我们称之为结构增强型端到端。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we go beyond the basic vanilla end-to-end by augmenting the learned embeddings with materialized structure representations.
zh: 所以我们通过用物化的结构表示来增强学习到的嵌入，超越了基本的原味端到端。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that gives us a few very important advantages.
zh: 这给了我们几个非常重要的优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: So first is validation at inference time.
zh: 所以首先是推理时的验证。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, because the model isn't just a black box where sensors go in and actuation commands go out, we can create a very powerful correctness and safety validation layer that you can run in real time when the agent is deployed on our vehicles.
zh: 现在，因为模型不仅仅是一个传感器进去、致动命令出来的黑盒，我们可以创建一个非常强大的正确性和安全验证层，当智能体部署在我们的车辆上时，你可以实时运行它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is really important for any agent that's operating in the physical world.
zh: 这对于任何在物理世界运行的智能体来说都非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Secondly,
zh: 其次，

speaker: Unknown
en: We get great wins in efficiency when it comes to large-scale training and evaluation of the generative part of the model, the decoder.
zh: 在大规模训练和评估模型的生成部分（即解码器）时，我们在效率方面取得了巨大的胜利。

speaker: Unknown
en: If all you have is a black box end-to-end system, you are forced to do all of your evaluation and all of your training in the end-to-end setup, all the way from sensors to decisions to actuation.
zh: 如果你只有一个黑盒端到端系统，你将被迫在端到端设置中完成所有的评估和所有的训练，一路从传感器到决策再到致动。

speaker: Unknown
en: Having that intermediate structured representation allows you to kind of mix and match.
zh: 拥有那种中间结构化表示允许你某种程度地混合和匹配。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can do some training at larger scale and some evaluation in the space of those compact structured representations and some in the full space of end-to-end from sensors to decisions.
zh: 你可以在更大的规模上做一些训练，并在那些紧凑结构化表示的空间中做一些评估，还有一些在从传感器到决策的完整端到端空间中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And finally, we get strong, verifiable feedback signals for both evaluation and for training recipes to support things like reinforcement learning.
zh: 最后，我们获得强大的、可验证的反馈信号，用于评估和训练配方，以支持诸如强化学习之类的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: That additional materialized structure just gives you much more powerful tools for evaluation, for metrics, as well as crafting your loss function or reinforcement learning recipes.
zh: 那种额外的物化结构只是为你提供了更强大的工具用于评估、用于指标，以及制作你的损失函数或强化学习配方。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the lesson here is to bet on a system that's maximally learned and minimally constrained and leverage structure intentionally to boost performance and scaling laws, both in training and in evaluation.
zh: 所以这里的教训是押注于一个最大限度地学习且最小程度受限的系统，并有意识地利用结构来提升性能和缩放定律，无论是在训练还是评估中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, that raises the question of how do you actually train and evaluate your physical AI agent?
zh: 现在，这就提出了一个问题，你实际上如何训练和评估你的物理 AI 智能体？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that brings us to the next lesson.
zh: 这带给我们下一个教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: To build...
zh: 要构建...

speaker: Unknown
en: And safely deploy an agent in the physical world, it is absolutely critical to have a good large-scale realistic high-fidelity simulator.
zh: 并在物理世界安全地部署一个智能体，拥有一个良好的大规模逼真高保真模拟器是绝对关键的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now there's two ways you can do training and evaluation.
zh: 现在有两种方法你可以做训练和评估。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can do open loop and you can do closed loop.
zh: 你可以做开环，你也可以做闭环。

speaker: Unknown
en: In open loop, you're kind of passively observing input to output pairs, and you can use that for evaluation, for training, imitation learning, works like that.
zh: 在开环中，你有点被动地观察输入输出对，你可以将其用于评估，用于训练，模仿学习，就像那样工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Evaluation takes usually the shape of, you know, if you were to find yourself in this situation, what would you do?
zh: 评估通常的形式是，如果你发现自己处于这种情况，你会做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you score that.
zh: 然后你对此打分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's in contrast with closed loop, where in closed loop, you take an action.
zh: 这与闭环形成对比，在闭环中，你采取一个行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: You see the effect that that action has on the world.
zh: 你看到该行动对世界产生的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then you update through your sensors the view of the world.
zh: 然后你通过你的传感器更新世界视图。

speaker: Unknown
en: You take another action and so forth and so on, and you evaluate and you train on those sequence of actions and sequence of world evolutions.
zh: 你采取另一个行动，依此类推，你进行评估，并基于那些动作序列和世界演变序列进行训练。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, the ability to take an action and evaluate that counterfactual is absolutely vital for building and deploying safety-critical agents in the physical world.
zh: 现在，采取行动并评估该反事实的能力，对于在物理世界中构建和部署安全关键智能体绝对至关重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a real simulator is how you do that.
zh: 所以真正的模拟器就是你做到这一点的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a real simulator isn't just some lightweight tooling that sits next to your AI.
zh: 而真正的模拟器不仅仅是一些位于你 AI 旁边的轻量级工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is a big AI model in of itself.
zh: 它本身就是一个大型 AI 模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the problem of building a good realistic simulator is just as hard as building the agent itself.
zh: 构建一个好的逼真模拟器的问题与构建智能体本身一样困难。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the AI behind the simulator really needs to understand how the world works, the physics, the semantics, the traffic, the weather, and so on and so forth.
zh: 所以模拟器背后的 AI 真的需要理解世界是如何运作的，物理、语义、交通、天气等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the quality of that simulator has to be high enough so that it doesn't only look good, but it's sufficient to train and evaluate with high confidence an agent that you're going to be putting in the world in a safety critical environment.
zh: 该模拟器的质量必须足够高，以至于它不仅看起来很好，而且足以让你高置信度地训练和评估你将要置于安全关键环境中的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in other words, you have to build a highly accurate generative world model.
zh: 换句话说，你必须构建一个高度准确的生成式世界模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at Waymo for years, we've been building what we called behavioral world models.
zh: 在 Waymo，多年来我们一直在构建我们所谓的行爲世界模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're doing that way before the term world models even became popular.
zh: 而且我们在“世界模型”这个词甚至变得流行之前很久就在这么做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now in the era of end-to-end models, you also need on top of behavioral realism, you need sensing realism as well.
zh: 现在在端到端模型的时代，除了行为真实感之外，你还需要感知真实感

speaker: Unknown
en: And in fact, building an end-to-end model has been fairly easy for quite a while now, but evaluating it in closed loop
zh: 事实上，构建端到端模型已经相当容易有一段时间了，但在闭环中评估它

speaker: Unknown
en: That was the hard part of the problem.
zh: 那是问题中困难的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we've moved on to building sensing world models.
zh: 所以我们已经转向构建传感世界模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And because we're using the structure-augmented representation in our models, we can also leverage that structure in our simulation.
zh: 因为我们在模型中使用了结构增强的表示，我们也可以在仿真中利用该结构。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our behavior world model operates in the space of structured intermediate representations, and the tightly coupled sensor world model then produces realistic sensor simulations.
zh: 我们的行为世界模型在结构化中间表示的空间中运作，紧密耦合的传感器世界模型随后生成逼真的传感器仿真。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our world model leverages the great work of Google DeepMinds on Genie 3, and that gives us the ability to produce controllable and highly realistic scenarios, both in the behavioral as well as sensing aspects.
zh: 我们的世界模型利用了 Google DeepMinds 在 Genie 3 上的杰出工作，这赋予了我们生成可控且高度逼真场景的能力，既包括行为方面也包括传感方面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that in turn allows us to not just evaluate our agent and train new versions of our agent in situations that we've previously encountered, but it allows us to train and evaluate in purely synthetic, rare scenarios that we've never seen in the real world.
zh: 这反过来不仅允许我们在我们以前遇到过的情况下评估我们的智能体并训练新版本的智能体，而且允许我们在我们在现实世界中从未见过的纯合成的、罕见的场景中训练和评估。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what you're seeing here is not just the generated video, it's a generative, a full generative simulation of the Waymo driver in operating closed loop.
zh: 所以这里你们看到的不仅仅是生成的视频，它是 Waymo 驾驶员在闭环操作中的生成式，一个完整的生成式仿真。

speaker: Unknown
en: So here we're simulating what would happen if it came across a car that was stopped in a lane on the freeway.
zh: 所以这里我们在仿真如果它遇到一辆在高速公路车道上停着的车会发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can go further than that.
zh: 而且你可以比那更进一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's a plane that's landing on a freeway in front of us.
zh: 这是一架正在我们前方高速公路上降落的飞机。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or you can simulate an elephant on the loose walking through the intersection.
zh: 或者你可以模拟一头乱跑的大象穿过路口。

speaker: Unknown
en: Snow on the Golden Gate Bridge or a dinosaur walking around.
zh: 金门大桥上的雪或四处走动的恐龙。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the lesson here is that closed-loop simulation is absolutely required for evaluation and is extremely valuable for training of your physical AI agents.
zh: 所以这里的教训是，闭环仿真对于评估是绝对必需的，对于训练你的物理 AI 智能体也是极其有价值的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you need highly realistic, large-scale simulation to train and evaluate.
zh: 所以你需要高度逼真的大规模仿真来训练和评估。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this brings us to lesson number six.
zh: 这把我们带进了第六个教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you're dealing
zh: 当你在处理

speaker: Unknown
en: With a problem of that complexity, you can't just build a model and call it a day.
zh: 如此复杂的问题时，你不能只是建立一个模型然后就完事了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to build an entire ecosystem.
zh: 你必须构建一个完整的生态系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you also need a flywheel that powers it.
zh: 然后你还需要一个驱动它的飞轮。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because to make this work at scale, you can't just build the agent and one AI, you need to build three.
zh: 因为要使其大规模运作，你不能只构建智能体和一个 AI，你需要构建三个。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're building the agent.
zh: 你正在构建智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: For us, that's the driver that drives the car.
zh: 对我们来说，那是驾驶汽车的驾驶员。

speaker: Unknown
en: You also have the simulator.
zh: 你还有仿真器。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which is that virtual playground for the agent to learn in.
zh: 那是智能体在里面学习的虚拟游乐场。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you have the critic.
zh: 然后你有评判者。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the critic is what rigorously evaluates and judges the performance of the agent and tells it how to improve.
zh: 评判者是严格评估和判断智能体的表现并告诉它如何改进的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the good news is that the fundamental reasoning and the generative capabilities of all three of those are shared.
zh: 好消息是，这三者的基本推理和生成能力是共享的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's why, in our case, they're based on the same foundation role model.
zh: 这就是为什么，在我们的案例中，它们基于相同的基础角色模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, once you have these three pillars, you can create an incredibly powerful flywheel to accelerate your progress.
zh: 现在，一旦你有了这三大支柱，你就可以创建一个极其强大的飞轮来加速你的进度。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a deployment of your agent in the real world generates data.
zh: 所以智能体在现实世界中的部署会产生数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: That data then grounds the simulator and makes it more realistic.
zh: 然后这些数据为仿真器提供基础并使其更逼真。

speaker: Unknown
en: The simulator generates harder age cases for the critic to score and for the agent to learn from.
zh: 仿真器为评判者打分和智能体从中学习生成更难的年龄案例。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the agent gets smarter, gets deployed in the physical world, generate more data, and that powers the flywheel and accelerates progress.
zh: 所以智能体变得更聪明，被部署在物理世界中，生成更多数据，这为飞轮提供动力并加速进步。

speaker: Unknown
en: But a flywheel, of course, will spin in any direction or in place.
zh: 但飞轮当然会向任何方向旋转或原地旋转。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in order to make it go in the direction you want, you need to guide it by metrics.
zh: 所以为了让它朝你想要的方向前进，你需要通过指标来引导它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that brings us to the final lesson that your model is really table stakes, but eval and metrics, that's your most important, that's your strategic mode.
zh: 这带给我们最后一个教训，你的模型真的是入场门槛，但评估和指标，那才是你最重要的东西，那是你的战略模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So build your eval before you build your technology.
zh: 所以在构建你的技术之前，先构建你的评估。

speaker: Unknown
en: Build your eval and your metrics before you build your product.
zh: 在构建你的产品之前，先构建你的评估和你的指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you can't quantitatively define what good enough means, you're not really building a product, you're just iterating on your demo.
zh: 如果你不能定量地定义“足够好”意味着什么，你并不是在构建产品，你只是在迭代你的演示。

speaker: Unknown
en: So nowadays, the best model architectures are fairly well known, and new ideas tend to proliferate fairly quickly.
zh: 所以如今，最好的模型架构是相当众所周知的，新想法往往传播得相当快。

speaker: Unknown
en: Data is incredibly important, but without good metrics, you're just flying blind.
zh: 数据极其重要，但没有好的指标，你只是在盲目飞行。

speaker: Unknown
en: You aren't leveraging the best data, and you can't really evaluate the ROI on making changes to it.
zh: 你没有利用最好的数据，你也无法真正评估对它进行更改的投资回报率（ROI）。

speaker: Unknown
en: So really, eval and metrics, that's your foundation, and that's what steers your whole tech stack.
zh: 所以真的，评估和指标，那是你的基础，那是你引导整个技术栈的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But for physical AI agents, model-level evaluation is not enough.
zh: 但对于物理 AI 智能体来说，模型级别的评估是不够的。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you're putting an AI agent into the physical world, your eval and your validation needs to go much deeper and much broader.
zh: 当你把一个 AI 智能体放入物理世界时，你的评估和你的验证需要深入得多和广泛得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to evaluate and validate every component of your system
zh: 你需要评估和验证你系统的每一个组件

speaker: Unknown
en: From the physical layer to the behavioral layer that's running on board in the physical world, as well as the off-board components and all of the operational processes around it.
zh: 从物理层到在物理世界中运行在板上的行为层，以及车外组件和围绕它的所有操作流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for us, we call that the safety and readiness framework.
zh: 所以对我们来说，我们称之为安全与准备框架。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we spent years building and refining it.
zh: 我们花了数年时间构建和完善它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what guides our development and our deployment and our scaling.
zh: 这正是指导我们开发、部署和扩展的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I consider that to be one of our most important assets.
zh: 我认为那是我们最重要的资产之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, the reason it's important is because in the physical world, trust is everything.
zh: 再次重申，它之所以重要的原因是因为在物理世界中，信任就是一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: And eval and metrics is how you go about earning that trust.
zh: 而评估和指标就是你赢得信任的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't just win trust by talking about the clever technical solution or the clever state-of-the-art architecture of your models.
zh: 你不能仅仅通过谈论巧妙的技术解决方案或模型的最先进架构来赢得信任。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or doing a Flasher demo.
zh: 或者做一个 Flasher 演示。

speaker: Unknown
en: You earn it gradually, day by day, in the field, by relentlessly proving that your system is safe and that your system works.
zh: 你是逐渐地，一天一天地，在现场，通过无情地证明你的系统是安全的并且你的系统是有效的来赢得它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And of course, you can just prove that to yourself behind closed doors.
zh: 当然，你可以只在门后向你自己证明这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is exactly why we openly publish our safety data and our safety, ongoing safety research.
zh: 这正是为什么我们要公开发布我们的安全数据和我们的安全，正在进行的 安全研究。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then that earned trust becomes your ultimate business advantage.
zh: 因此，那种赢得的信任成为了你终极的商业优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your models can be leaked, algorithms can be replicated, but hundreds of millions of miles of fully autonomous operations in the real world, backed by evidence-grade evaluation and publicly audited proof, that is much, much more difficult to replicate.
zh: 你的模型可能会被泄露，算法可能会被复制，但在现实世界中数亿英里的完全自主操作，由证据级评估和公开审计证明支持，这要难得多、得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when you zoom out and look at this playbook as a whole, you realize that none of these lessons works alone.
zh: 所以当你缩小视角并将这本剧本作为一个整体来看时，你会意识到这些教训中没有一个是单独起作用的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the nines set your bar and ensure that you pick the right technology and the right technical approach so that you don't get stuck on the local minimum.
zh: 所以那个“九”设定了你的标准并确保你选择了正确的技术和正确的技术方法，这样你就不会被困在局部最小值上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then intentional use of structure to boost scaling and the ability to arrive technical waves of innovation helps you get to the right level of nines.
zh: 然后，有意识地利用结构来提升扩展性以及到达技术创新浪潮的能力帮助你达到正确的“九”的水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: And your AI ecosystem with the agent, the simulator, and the critic guided by your eval and metrics, that's what allows you to build that powerful flywheel.
zh: 还有你的 AI 生态系统，包括智能体、模拟器和由评估和指标引导的评判者，这就是让你构建那个强大飞轮的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's how all of these effects compound.
zh: 这就是所有这些效应复合在一起的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's this playbook that we've been refining over the years is what allows us to achieve the strongly superhuman safety performance of the Waymo driver.
zh: 正是我们多年来一直在完善的这个剧本，使我们能够实现 Waymo 驾驶员的强超人安全性能。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a snapshot of the latest safety data we've released.
zh: 这是我们发布的最新安全数据的快照。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's based on over 220 million fully autonomous miles.
zh: 它基于超过 2.2 亿英里的完全自主里程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're seeing there that in the areas where we operate, the Waymo driver is about 17 times better than human drivers when it comes to crashes that cause serious injury.
zh: 我们在那里看到，在我们运营的区域，Waymo 驾驶员在导致严重伤害的碰撞方面比人类驾驶员大约好 17 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that really matters because today, somewhere in the world, every 26 seconds, someone loses their lives on a road to a crash event.
zh: 这真的很重要，因为今天，在世界的某个地方，每 26 秒，就有某人在道路上因一次碰撞事件而丧生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And on the current scale, what that means is that Waymo is preventing a serious injury every eight days.
zh: 按照目前的规模，这意味着 Waymo 每八天就能预防一次严重伤害。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this isn't just a metric on a dashboard.
zh: 这不仅仅是仪表盘上的一个指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: That means that someone's loved one got to walk through the front door at the end of the day safe and unharmed.
zh: 这意味着某人的亲人在一天结束时能够安全无恙地走进前门。

speaker: Unknown
en: So these are just the early safety benefits of AI in the physical world, and they will only grow from there.
zh: 所以这些只是物理世界中 AI 的早期安全益处，它们只会从那里增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you look at the broader landscape, the opportunity here is absolutely massive.
zh: 如果你看看更广阔的前景，这里的机会绝对是巨大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Physical AI right now is where digital AI was a few years ago, and we have all of the right ingredients to go after it.
zh: 物理 AI 现在就处于数字 AI 几年前的位置，而且我们拥有所有正确的要素去追求它。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have degenerative world models, we have the architectures, we have affordable compute and sensing, we have proven scaling laws, and we have a real product operating at scale.
zh: 我们有退化世界模型，我们有架构，我们有负担得起的计算和感知，我们有经证实的缩放定律，我们有一个大规模运营的真实产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the last decade of AI happened in the digital world.
zh: 过去十年的 AI 发生在数字世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the next decade will also happen in the physical world.
zh: 我认为下一个十年也将发生在物理世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for those of you who decide to build in this space, good luck, have fun.
zh: 对于那些决定在这个领域建设的人来说，祝好运，玩得开心。

speaker: Unknown
en: And remember who you're building for.
zh: 并且记住你是在为谁构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your mission and your customers, that's what matters.
zh: 你的使命和你的客户，那才是重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Otherwise, tech is just a science project.
zh: 否则，技术只是一个科学项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at the end of the day, as exciting, as exhilarating the tech is, nothing really beats the joy of making a difference in people's lives.
zh: 归根结底，尽管这项技术多么令人兴奋、多么激动人心，没有什么能真正胜过对人们的生活产生影响所带来的喜悦。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are we doing?
zh: 我们在做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: We're in our first ever Waymo.
zh: 我们在我们生平第一辆 Waymo 里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what does it mean when we're in a Waymo?
zh: 当我们在一辆 Waymo 里时，这意味着什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: It means that there is nobody driving this thing!
zh: 这意味着没有人正在驾驶这个东西！

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is a fully autonomous Waymo ride.
zh: 这是一次完全自主的 Waymo 行程。

speaker: Unknown
en: I cannot believe this!
zh: 我简直不敢相信这个！

speaker: Unknown
en: The car did a better job than if somebody was driving!
zh: 这辆车表现得比如果有人在驾驶还要好！

speaker: Unknown
en: The truck was over the yellow line, so the Waymo braked and moved to the side.
zh: 那辆卡车越过了黄线，所以 Waymo 刹了车并移到了一侧。

speaker: Unknown
en: It knew how to pronounce my name!
zh: 它知道如何读我的名字！

speaker: Unknown
en: This is so cool.
zh: 这太酷了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll never forget this.
zh: 我永远不会忘记这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Never.
zh: 永远不会。
